title: Review of Intelligent Tutoring Systems Using Bayesian Approach
extended_summary:
This paper reviews intelligent tutoring systems (ITS) with a focus on how Bayesian networks can be used to support uncertainty management and decision making in tutoring environments. Rather than reporting a new empirical study, it explains the core architecture of ITSs, including knowledge base, student model, teaching model, and control engine, and discusses why Bayesian networks are useful for modeling incomplete or uncertain information about learner knowledge.

The paper surveys several ITS examples, including Andes, ViSMod, and BITS, to illustrate how Bayesian networks have been used for student modeling, predicting learner actions, and selecting instructional strategies. These systems are described as adaptive environments that represent domain concepts and student performance probabilistically, allowing the system to update beliefs about what the learner knows and to tailor feedback or next steps accordingly.

The context is broad rather than tied to one classroom, grade level, or country. The paper emphasizes that ITSs can be used in traditional classrooms or distance learning and across domains such as physics and programming. Its main conclusion is that Bayesian networks offer a strong formal framework for intelligent tutoring because they support probabilistic inference, adaptive instruction, and flexible student modeling under uncertainty.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a narrative review/framework paper rather than an empirical evaluation. It summarizes prior ITS work and Bayesian-network applications but does not report a new study design, sample, or effect estimates.
impact_tier_rationale: No measurable intervention effect is reported in this paper. The article is descriptive and theoretical, so there is no evidence of impact on learner outcomes in the text provided.

interventions.use_case: review of Bayesian-network-based intelligent tutoring systems for adaptive student modeling, diagnosis, and decision-making in tutoring (e.g., Andes, ViSMod, BITS)
